feedback.problem: The line $y=x-k$ intersects the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}-k,$ where $k\ne 0,$ twice. What is the range of possible values of  $k?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To determine whether the line $y=x-k$ intersects the hyperbola $y=\frac{k}{x}-k,$ we need to solve the following system of equations for the two curves:  

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=x-k &  \\ y=\frac{k}{x}-k\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and simplifying, we get a quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-k & =\frac{k}{x}-k \\ x-k & =\frac{k-kx}{x} \\ x(x-k) & =k-kx \\ {x}^{2} & =k \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{k}\end{aligned}
$$

In order for the line to intersect the hyperbola at two points, the quadratic formula above must give two real solutions.

So, the expression inside the square root must be positive: 

$$
\begin{aligned}k & >0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the range of possible values of $k$ is $k\in (0,\infty ).$
